headline: No 64–68 break in range — warm water, fog, closing window
body:
Lead with the fog: both mornings carry patchy dense fog, visibility a mile or less — run slow on radar and AIS until it lifts. Monday the Channel is easy, 2 ft inside and 2.6 at the triangle middle, west wind filling to 10 kn gusting 16 by mid-afternoon; the far grounds are workable, Osborn and San Nic near 3.3–3.6 ft, Santa Rosa Flats rougher at 13–19 kn WNW. Tuesday the Channel holds (2–3 ft) but the outer waters blow out — Santa Rosa 20–21 kn gusting 25 at 4.3 ft, San Nic gusting 21.

The bluefin call is a hard one: there's no 64–68 water anywhere on the chart. Every ground reads 70–73°F, well north of the red isotherm. The break has slid off north and west, beyond even Santa Rosa Flats, which at 70.9–71.4 is the coolest water in range. Inside the triangle the coolest corner is the west, south of Santa Cruz — 72.5 today, 71.1 Tuesday; east and south points sit near 73. Neither day is a true break day. If you go, Monday's the window; work the west corner, but temper the plan.
